portfolio.title: budgIT
portfolio.overview: budgIT is a budgeting concept designed for Finnish university students, with wireframes and mockups presented in Finnish. It helps students manage expenses, budgets, savings goals, and overall financial awareness across mobile and desktop. Created for a Human–Technology Interaction course, the project covered the full UX process from user research and information architecture to interaction design and high-fidelity prototyping.
portfolio.problem: Students often face irregular income, high living costs, and limited experience with financial planning. Interviews showed that most rely on banking apps for basic tracking but lack simple tools for proactive budgeting, clear overviews, and student-focused guidance. Existing finance apps were often seen as too complex or poorly suited to student life.
portfolio.solution:
We designed budgIT as a lightweight financial hub for students, focused on clarity and ease of use. The concept combines budgeting, expense tracking, savings goals, student loans, and discounts in one simple experience.

I was mainly responsible for building and visually refining the interactive prototype while contributing throughout the design process.
portfolio.researchInsight: Interviews with university students helped us identify three main needs:
researchInsightPoints: Clear financial information at a glance
Simple tools for irregular income and expenses
Student-focused guidance without complex financial language
portfolio.structureInteraction: We designed a content structure where the primary navigation is organized around a high-level overview and clear feature groups, allowing users to access deeper details without cluttering the main view.
portfolio.structureToVisualText: After defining the information architecture, we translated the structure into low-fidelity wireframes. These iterations helped validate hierarchy, grouping, and clarity before moving into high-fidelity visual design.
portfolio.outcome: The final result was an interactive prototype that clearly visualizes monthly budgets, expenses, and remaining funds, supports savings goals and basic financial learning, and adapts to different screen sizes and usage situations. Peer feedback highlighted the clarity, usability, and visual structure of the solution. The project demonstrated how user research can directly shape interaction design and lead to a more approachable financial tool for a specific user group.

persona.name: Mikko
persona.goal: Manage finances clearly and save money without giving up student life.
persona.quote: I want to understand my finances quickly, without feeling restricted or overwhelmed.

beforeAfter.title: Before & After Navigation
beforeAfter.note: Side-by-side wireframe vs final UI highlighting icon-based navigation for accessibility and scannability.

portfolio.collaboration: We coordinated via Telegram for rapid feedback and divided responsibilities while keeping a shared vision.
impactLearnings: How to translate qualitative research into concrete UI decisions
How to design financial information without overwhelming users
The importance of iteration and content hierarchy in dashboards
Working in a multidisciplinary team with shared design ownership
portfolio.uxDecision: Based on user feedback, we moved charts above detailed lists to reduce cognitive load and help users quickly understand their financial situation.
portfolio.reflection: If continued, I would validate the design with usability testing and explore real-time data syncing across devices.

portfolio.title: AllTogether
portfolio.description: workouts, sleep, recovery, and nutrition in one mobile experience.
portfolio.challenge: People who care about their health often use multiple apps and devices to track workouts, sleep, recovery, and nutrition. The result is fragmented data and poor overview - users know they are tracking, but not necessarily how they are doing. Our goal was to design a single mobile experience that brings this information together in a way that feels motivating, clear, and easy to understand at a glance.
portfolio.myRoleSummary: I worked as a UX/UI designer in a small team, contributing especially to:
myRolePoints: Defining the product vision and target users
Designing the mobile home screen focused on data clarity
Refining visual hierarchy, spacing, and UX writing
Evolving the design into a high-fidelity mobile UI
portfolio.userUnderstanding: We designed for 20-40-year-old health-conscious users who want to track their wellbeing without feeling overwhelmed by numbers or complex tools.
userDecisionAnchors: Showing insights instead of raw data
portfolio.visionSummary: Early on, we aligned on a clear vision: a mobile-first, all-in-one health app where users understand their daily status within seconds of opening the app.
visionPriorities: Modular content that can grow over time
Social features that feel supportive, not competitive
portfolio.wireframesSummary: We designed a simple navigation flow that always brings the user back to a clear overview. In the wireframing phase, we explored different dashboard layouts and tested how much information could be shown without overwhelming the user.
portfolio.wireframesInsight: Through iteration, it became clear that fewer, well-prioritized metrics worked better than dense data views.
finalExperiencePoints: Glanceable activity, sleep, and recovery data
Card-based layout for clarity and flexibility
Calm colors and increased white space
Familiar interaction patterns to reduce friction
Optional dark mode for real-world usage
portfolio.finalExperienceResult: The result is a mobile UI that feels informative but calm - something users can quickly check during everyday routines.
portfolio.outcome: The final concept delivers a cohesive mobile experience that combines fitness, nutrition, recovery, and social motivation into one interface. The project reinforced how much impact visual hierarchy, spacing, and prioritization have when designing data-heavy products.
portfolio.reflection: If continued, the next steps would include usability testing with real users and deeper validation of how users interpret the shown metrics.
